content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model fails to capture sharp downside moves.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays mean reversion after spikes, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Overshoot after spikes: model frequently forecasts a peak too high after a sharp rise, then undercorrects.
- Horizon bias: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate mid-term volatility, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is > 0.0, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per 0.10 sentiment unit; if sentiment < -0.30, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per 0.10 unit.
